source.title: Do VLMs Share Safety Neurons Across Modalities?
source.authors: Jia-Xuan Li; Jia-Hao Zhang; D. Vo; H. Nguyen; Pride Kavumba; Koki Wataoka

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study refines the localization claim using neuron-set ablations and GEVD projections rather than the original single difference-in-means residual direction. It reports text effects concentrated in a few directions and visual effects that grow through 50 directions, with modality-specific neuron-ablation results.
record.gate_note: The study tests causal safety interventions in VLM backbones, but does not implement the original difference-in-means residual direction. Neuron counts used during detection and the candidate-selection probe scores are not recorded as outcome rows. The behavioral factorial refusal rates in Table 2 and Appendix D are not included as claim-version rows because they do not test the proposed direction or its transfer. The study reports additional per-model comparisons of text- and visual-neuron ablation in Table 5 and additional GEVD results in Appendix G; these are omitted under the 60-row cap, as explained below.
record.test_reason: Most of the paper ablates neuron sets, which is not the direction named by V1 or V4. Only the GEVD analysis (Sec. 5.4, Table 6, App. G.1) tests the claim. It projects out k linear directions separating harmful from safe representations at one layer, with a random-direction null, and measures refusal. That is a different method aimed at the same question: is refusal mediated by one or a few linear directions? The setting is VLM backbones, with text and visual harmful inputs.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that text safety is localized to about 88 neurons on average and saturates within about 5 GEVD directions, and that these neurons are the dominant refusal pathway, including for image-borne harm. They see visual safety as diffuse at the neuron level, with little consistent OOD transfer, and as needing ≥50 directions where measurable. They add that 'diffuse' does not mean absent and that not all visual safety mechanisms need be diffuse.
record.recipe_differences: The original studies a single residual-stream direction derived from harmful-minus-harmless mean activations. This paper uses behavior-conditioned neuron screening, safe-mean activation patching, iterative neuron-set ablation, and GEVD projection sweeps at selected layers; it does not add a direction. The paper says it releases no per-model neuron coordinate lists or turnkey ablation code.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by modality, model, stimulus distribution, and intervention size. Text-neuron effects occur on IID and Do-Not-Answer OOD prompts; visual-neuron effects show weak or mixed OOD transfer. GEVD effects depend on modality and k, and visual refusal changes are not stable across queries. The RR-Judge versus RR-KW comparison also varies across models and query distributions.

fits_no_version.finding: Text refusal in 10 VLM backbones is partly localized to 48–130 MLP/attention neurons. Clamping them to safe-query means lowers refusal by 9–33 pp IID and 2–21 pp on OOD Do-Not-Answer queries. PPL shift is ≤7.4%, and MMLU moves by ≤0.3 pp in 7 models. For some models the effect is mostly on phrasing (RR-J/RR-KW ratio 0.09–1.88).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal on text harmful inputs can be substantially reduced by ablating a sparse neuron set (~0.01% of neurons) in VLM language backbones.

fits_no_version.finding: Visual-input refusal yields only 0–9 confirmed neurons. Their ablation reduces IID refusal by 2.8–40 pp but has no consistent OOD effect (|∆|<4 pp in 7 of 8 models, with mixed signs).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image-triggered refusal in VLMs is not localized to a few backbone neurons, and depends mainly on the text-safety neuron pathway.

record.problems: The paper notes that interventions target only the LLM backbone; 82.5% of retained V I S AFE-D ETECT harmful images come from BeaverTails-V; the factorial benchmark selects 472 intents for high text-only refusal consensus; and RR-Judge uses one judge model. RR-Judge versus keyword refusal comparisons show that some text-neuron ablation effects may affect canonical phrasing more than the refusal decision. General-capability results are reported only on selected benchmarks and subsets.
record.rows_left_out: Under the 60-row cap, omitted Table 5's per-model, per-intervention comparisons for procedural-query-plus-harmful-image and direct-harmful-query conditions. Those cells compare text- and visual-neuron ablations and include model-specific sign changes; Table 5 is in Section 5.4. Also omitted the remaining k-sweep entries in Table 6 and the per-model GEVD k=5/k=50 results in Appendix G, Table G.1. Text neuron counts are reported in Table 3 and visual neuron counts in Table 4; counts for nonzero sets are noted alongside the corresponding ablation rows rather than given separate measurement rows.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is used. There is no ablation across all layers and positions, no direction addition to induce refusal, and no single-direction test beyond Qwen2.5-VL-7B among the rows. Capability checks (PPL/MMLU/MMMU) are reported only for neuron ablation.
No weight edit or abliteration of released models.
No analysis of jailbreaks suppressing the direction and no adversarial training.
Affine or cone formulations are not tested. Text direction effects are too small to show how many directions are involved.
Harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are not separated.
No transfer of directions across languages, model variants, or base to instruct. The text-versus-image modality contrast is not transfer of the same direction.
Thinking models (Qwen3.5-9B-Thinking, GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking) appear only in neuron ablations. GLM's GEVD text result (App. G.1) has no random null and no reasoning-stage analysis.

missing.what: Visual GEVD k=1 (−30 pp vs null −5) and the random-direction null column for all k. These are needed as rows and baselines for the V1 and V4 verdicts. Partly covered by the 'remaining k-sweep' declaration, but the null is required to read any GEVD row.

GEVD text k5/k50 for other models, especially GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking (−48/−52 pp), a large text-direction effect in a reasoning model. Also visual k5→k50 growth in Qwen3-VL-2B/8B/32B, reported without a null. Declared as omitted, but it bears on V1, V4 and V8.

record.verdict_notes: The neuron-level core of the paper does not test a direction claim, so those rows are delinked and placed under fits_no_version. Table 6 columns were reconstructed from the flattened text. Text: ∆KW, ∆PPL (+1083 at k=500), Rand-k. Visual: ∆KW, ∆PPL, Rand-k. This reading is checked against the paper's stated net values (−22 at k=5, −28 at k=50). Under this reading the text GEVD effects are near null at every k≤100. The visual effect is mostly present at k=1 once the null is subtracted, which weakens the paper's own '≥50 directions' interpretation. No V8 verdict is given, because thinking models appear only in neuron ablations and in the omitted G.1 data without a null.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not find and ablate the original single difference-in-means residual-stream direction at every layer and position, and does not add that direction to induce refusals on harmless requests. It tests neuron-set interventions and GEVD projections instead.
No conversion of the intervention into a weight edit or evaluation of released-model abliteration.
No test of whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.

The study tests GEVD subspace scaling and neuron-level localization, but does not test affine or cone models specifically, nor whether a dominant direction plus additional directions is the best formal description.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
The study includes multiple models and architectures but does not transfer a discovered direction between languages, model variants, or base and instruct checkpoints.
Adapted and natively multimodal architectures are compared, but the study does not vary when or how refusal training is performed.
Thinking variants are included, but the study does not test the original single-direction intervention in reasoning models or analyze reasoning-stage activations.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-VL-7B
rows.operation_detail: Projected out the top GEVD direction at the best text layer.
rows.note: A single GEVD direction produced a small measured change; this is not the original difference-in-means direction.
rows.check: The baseline should be the random-direction null at k=1 (−1 pp RR-KW). The GEVD effect (−1) equals the null. This is one GEVD direction at one layer (L12), not a difference-in-means direction ablated at all layers.

source_check.correct: Baseline: the random-direction null (Rand-k, mean of 5 seeds) at k=1 is -1 pp, so the net effect is 0. The pre-ablation RR-KW refusal rate is not stated.
source_check.problem: The text gives a random-direction null for this cell, so 'not stated' is wrong. Value -1 equals the null, so 'absent' is right.
